audit.why: Content chart Gnar / Skill / Gragas / Gragas / Gnar / Gragas / Gragas differs from the packet only at Level 2 (packet Gnar, page Skill), and the page's own whys[1] describes a free chunk for Gnar. I left it: a chart flip must be proposed as a whole group and both layers already agree, so a single-row change would be held back anyway and the 46.3% win rate does not argue for giving Gnar more.
Four spikes present and real: Lvl 2 poke, Lvl 6 Rage window, Lvl 3-5 Body Slam window, first-item sustain. Cooldown detail added to spikes[3] rather than restructuring.
audit.corrected: Barrel Roll's 6s rank-5 cooldown added to spikes[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: The page credits Gragas's healing to Drunken Rage (W) in five places. Riot's W description contains no heal — it gives magic damage on the next basic attack and damage reduction. The heal is Happy Hour (P), which triggers on ability casts.
audit.why: This misdirects the reader's anti-heal thinking: the sustain is not tied to the 5s W drink, it comes off every spell he casts, so Grievous Wounds matters against his whole rotation rather than one button. The W is also an auto-attack reset, making the drink the burst tell.
audit.corrected: Heal re-attributed to Happy Hour in wants.foe[1], whys[5] and spikes[3]; Drunken Rage left as damage reduction plus the empowered-attack tell in Key Ability Interactions.

enemyKit Gragas W text and autoReset flag

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere — 'His engage. Mega-CC after it.' gives the reader nothing to count.
audit.why: Body Slam is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12 and Barrel Roll 10/9/8/7/6. 13s at rank 3 is the size of the window with no gap-close.
audit.corrected: Both numbers written into the cooldown block, the do's and Key Ability Interactions.

notes: No mirror audit existed for gragas__gnar, so this side is the first pass — when it is written it should restate the same facts inverted: Gnar ahead Lvl 1-2 and at 6 with Mega banked, Gragas ahead Lvl 3-5 and from first item, heal sourced to Happy Hour not Drunken Rage. suspectNames flagged 'Body Slams' in spikes[1] — that is the correct ability name pluralised as a verb, a false positive, left alone. The heal wording still survives in early, mid and late prose; I fixed the three shortest carriers plus the two full-layer blocks and left the long paragraphs alone rather than risk the length band on a rewrite that changes only attribution.
